headline: Spatial transcriptomics cleanup and lean perturbation models stress reliability
label: Spatial Imputation And Perturbation Models
summary: New preprints address transcript spillover, noise-aware histology metrics and imputation, while linear and additive models probe perturbation prediction limits.
synthesis: The largest thread is spatial transcriptomics, where several methods address data artefacts and reliable evaluation. Dancer separates within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination, and SYNDRI removes transcript spillover with a supervised transformer trained on simulated data. For histology-to-expression inference, reproducible-signal correlation (RSC) splits RNA counts to separate reproducible signal from noise, and REGAIN attaches per-prediction confidence before TCGA-BRCA prognostic analysis. ARC-Impute regularises cell-to-spot mapping and ranks first across 17 human and mouse datasets, while SCATTER and GaLF-ST address deconvolution and reconstruction. A second thread concerns perturbation response modelling with deliberately constrained structure. BiPert tests how far a linear decomposition into shared and perturbation-specific components extends to unseen contexts. GAIN models combinatorial responses as an additive baseline plus a learned interaction term, CIRCE infers graded signaling activity from combinatorial label structure, and CMC-VAE refines perturbation predictions through interventions on a CITE-seq causal latent space.
